{{Short description|Chinese-American physicist}}
{{BLP sources|date=January 2012}}

'''Tsao Chang''' ({{zh|s=张操}}; born 1942 in [[Shanghai, China]]) is a Chinese-American physicist.<ref>[http://www.hudong.com/wiki/%E5%BC%A0%E6%93%8D Tsao Chang] Hudong. (Chinese). Retrieved December 26, 2011.</ref>

Chang has taught physics and conducted research on the theory of space and time for more than fifty years in China and the United States.

== Personal life ==
Tsao Chang was born in Shanghai, China, on April 22, 1942. He met his wife, Bei Lei Dong, while attending [[Fudan University]]. They were wed in September 1967 and had two children, both sons. Their eldest son, John Zhang, became a successful business man and a member of the board for several public companies.<ref>{{Cite web|title = John Zhang: Executive Profile & Biography - Businessweek|url=https://www.bloomberg.com/research/stocks/private/person.asp?personId=37373073&privcapId=100495355|website = Businessweek.com|accessdate = 2016-01-06}}</ref>  Chang’s younger son, James Zhang is founder and CEO of Concept Art House, a video game developer.<ref>{{Cite web|title = About Us|url=http://www.conceptarthouse.com/about-us/|website = Concept Art House {{!}} Game Art Outsourcing|accessdate = 2016-01-06}}</ref>

== Physics career ==
In 1965, Chang graduated from [[Fudan University]], China with a degree in [[nuclear physics]].<ref>[http://www.chinadaily.com.cn/hqgj/jryw/2011-11-25/content_4482689.html China Daily interview]{{dead link|date=October 2025}}</ref>

Chang has taught [[electrodynamics]] and modern physics in China and the [[United States]]. From 1980 to 1982, he was a visiting scholar in the physics department at the [[University of Massachusetts Amherst]]. He also taught in the department of physics, [[Shanghai University]] of Science and Technology from 1982–1985. From 1985–1989, Chang was a visiting professor at both [[Utah State University]] and the [[University of Alabama]] in the United States.{{citation needed|date=December 2011}} From 1989–2002, Chang conducted research on space physics at Alabama.

Chang's research areas cover [[superluminal]] [[neutrinos]] and the [[theory of relativity]].<ref>[http://en.scientificcommons.org/tsao_chang]{{dead link|date=October 2025}}</ref> He has produced more than thirty research papers in addition to two books.<ref>[http://www.sstlp.com/book/detail.aspx?Id=2192 Tsao Chang,  "Research on the theory of Space and Time"]</ref>

In an international conference "in early 1985, T. Chang predicted neutrinos may be Superluminal particles".<ref>T. Chang,"Does a free [[tachyon]] exist ?", Proceedings of the Sir A. Eddington Centenary Symposium, (1986), Vol. 3,  Gravitational Radiation and Relativity", p.431.</ref>

Since 2002, his research has centered on the theory of space and time.
